forbes_bio: Julian Baker is a cofounder of Baker Brothers Advisors, a New York hedge fund that specializes in biotechnology stocks.

name: Koos Bekker
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Koos Bekker is revered for transforming South African newspaper publisher Naspers into an e-commerce investor and cable TV powerhouse.
He led Naspers to pay a reported $34 million for a third of Chinese Internet firm Tencent Holdings in 2001--perhaps the greatest venture investment ever.
In 2019, Naspers put some assets into two publicly-traded companies, entertainment firm MultiChoice Group and Prosus, which contains the Tencent stake
Naspers has sold down its stake in Tencent over the years and today owns less than 25%.
Bekker, who retired as the CEO of Naspers in March 2014, returned as chairman in April 2015.
forbes_facts: His Babylonstoren estate, nearly 600 acres in South Africa's Western Cape region, features architecture dating back to 1690, a farm, orchard and vineyard and more.

name: Sergei Popov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2004-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2016)
forbes_bio: Sergei Popov has cashed out of all his major investments in recent years.
He and his former partner Andrei Melnichenko made a fortune managing finance and industrial group MDM.
They later created TMK, one of the world's largest oil and gas pipe manufacturers, with fellow billionaire Dmitry Pumpyansky.
They sold out to Pumpyansky in 2006. That same year the partners started to divide up their assets, a process completed in 2012.
In 2015 he sold MDM Bank to Russia's Binbank. Two years later it went bankrupt and came under the control of the Central Bank of the Russian Federation.
forbes_facts: Popov is a founder of a private fund called Agat, which has a mentoring program that offers young businesspeople startup capital.
Popov hired a special public relations agency to help him stay out of the press.

name: Manohar Lal Agarwal
name_chinese: 马诺哈尔·拉尔·阿加瓦尔
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun India (2018-2019)
forbes_bio: Manohar Lal Agarwal, who was running Delhi-based Haldiram Foods, merged his company with Nagpur-based Haldiram Foods International in 2023 to create Haldiram Snacks Food.
A consortium of investors led by Singapore's Temasek, acquired a 20% stake in the merged company in 2025 at an estimated valuation of $10 billion.
Agarwal is the grandson of founder Ganga Bishan Agarwal, who started selling snacks from a tiny shop in Bikaner in Rajasthan in 1937 and went on to create the popular Haldiram brand.
The business was eventually divided among the patriarch's grandsons into three separate companies, operating out of Nagpur, Delhi and Kolkata.
forbes_facts: Haldiram Snacks has backed Venture Catalysts, an incubator, to invest in startups in packaged foods.

name: Sam Chong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Malaysian-born Sam Chong is the co-owner of Jellinbah Group, which operates two coal mines in Queensland.
Chong trained as a mining engineer in Taiwan before moving to Australia in 1972.
Sam and his son Paul are directors at Jellinbah Group.
In January 2025, Chong bought Anglo American's one-third stake in Jellinbah for A$1.6 billion ($1.1 billion); later in June 2025 he sold a 6.7% stake to Japanese conglomerate Marubeni.
Chong also owns a string of hotel and office properties in Brisbane.

name: Helena Dassault
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Helena Dassault is the daughter of Olivier Dassault, an heir to the Dassault aerospace and software fortune.
Olivier Dassault's grandfather founded Dassault Aviation, a French aerospace company that started out making propellers in World War I.
Her father Olivier, a prominent French politician who served as a representative in France's National Assembly, died in a helicopter crash in 2021.
The Dassault family also own the country's daily newspaper Le Figaro, several vineyards and a private aeronautic company.
Her brother Remi is also a billionaire.
forbes_facts: She studied acting and theatre at the Actors Factory and is following an acting career.

name: Liu Gexin

forbes_bio: Liu Gexin chairs Sichuan Kelun Pharmaceutical, a maker of antibiotics and traditional Chinese medicine.
Liu set up Kelun Pharmaceutical Factory, the predecessor company of Sichuan Kelun Pharmaceutcal, in 1996.
Kelun went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2010.

name: Katsumi Tada
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Katsumi Tada is the founder of property developer Daito Trust Construction, which specializes in building rental apartments.
In 2011, Tada stepped down as chairman and sold his stake back to the publicly traded company.
He switched his focus to Australia, where he develops and owns office buildings, malls and hotels through his privately held Daisho Co.
Daisho has a portfolio of 10 properties in Japan and overseas, including in Tokyo, Okinawa, Sydney, Brisbane, Melbourne and Singapore.
Tada also owns seven hotels in Japan.

name: Barry Bentley
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Barry Bentley and his brother Keith founded infrastructure engineering software provider Bentley Systems in 1984.
The company, which went public in 2020, develops and sells computer-aided design (CAD) software for architects and engineers working on public and industrial infrastructure.
A third brother, Greg, served as CEO for more than two decades before transitioning into the role of executive chair and president in 2024.
A fourth brother, Raymond, serves as a director.
The $1.5 billion (2025 sales) company remains majority owned by the Bentley family.
forbes_facts: The Bentley brothers' mom, Bonnie, was a schoolteacher and would make them read for an hour after lunch every day during the summer.
The first program Barry ever wrote on a computer was a blackjack game.

name: Brian Sheth
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2016-2020); Hurun Global (2017-2024); Wikidata (2020)
forbes_bio: Brian Sheth cofounded private equity firm Vista Equity Partners in 2000 with  Robert Smith.
Sheth oversees all deal-making at Vista, which has in recent years conducted more software acquisitions than any other company or investor.
Prior to launching Vista, where he serves as president, Sheth worked at Bain Capital, Goldman Sachs and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
He received a Bachelor of Science degree in economics from the University of Pennsylvania.
Sheth is chairman of Global Wildlife Conservation, an environmental foundation based in Austin, Texas.
forbes_facts: Sheth grew up lower-middle class in a Boston suburb; his father is an immigrant from India and his mother Irish-Catholic.
